verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down on Friday, April 10, 2026, at approximately 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown around 8:07 p.m. (5:07 p.m. PDT) Friday, April 10'; R3: 'splash down near San Diego at 5:07 p.m. PST on Friday, April 10'; R6: 'final splashdown at 5.07pm PT'; R7: 'splash down off San Diego at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state the exact date, time in PDT/EDT, and 'approximately' matches the phrasing.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule carrying four astronauts will land in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown ... off the coast of San Diego'; R2: 'splashed down off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splash down off San Diego’s coast'; R5: 'splash down ... off the coast of San Diego, California'; R7: 'splash down off San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant references explicitly confirm the location as Pacific Ocean off San Diego coast with four astronauts aboard Orion.

verifications.claim: Recovery operations will be conducted by the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'flown to the USS John P. Murtha. Recovery teams will retrieve the crew'; R2: 'delivered via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha'; R3: 'Navy sailors on the USS John P. Murtha will be responsible for recovering'; R8: 'airlifted to the USS John P. Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly name USS John P. Murtha as the recovery ship for operations post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: Live coverage begins on NASA+ and YouTube at 3:30 p.m. PDT / 6:30 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'mission status briefing is at 3:30 p.m. ... on ... YouTube channel'; 'Watch live return coverage on NASA+ ... starting at 6:30 p.m.'; R7: 'stream live coverage starting at 6:30 p.m. EDT on NASA+, ... YouTube'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm coverage on NASA+ and YouTube starting at 6:30 p.m. EDT (equivalent to 3:30 p.m. PDT), with briefing at 3:30 p.m. on YouTube aligning closely.

verifications.claim: Re-entry will involve a communication blackout during peak heating before parachutes deploy to bring the crew safely to the water.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'enter a planned six‑minute communications blackout at 7:53 p.m. as plasma forms around the capsule during peak heating'; 'deploy its drogue parachutes ... at 8:03 p.m., and then ... main parachutes ... at 8:04 p.m. to slow the capsule for splashdown'; R7: 'six-minute communications blackout during peak heating, deploy parachutes'
verifications.reasoning: References directly describe blackout during peak heating followed by parachute deployment for safe splashdown.
